answer: A mechanism that actually bites: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because shale only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, pulse is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any haven approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
